title: Retrieving Metrological Information from Noisy Squeezed Spin States via Bayesian Optimization
authors: Enze Li, Yunjie Cai, Jingwei Zhang, Emi Yukawa
abstract: Frequency inhomogeneity can obscure the metrological advantage of squeezed spin states, making the choice of readout crucial. We study interacting spin-1/2 ensembles with static local frequency disorder and optimize a common collective readout over independent disorder realizations. Using Bayesian optimization of the full measurement-outcome distribution, we identify observables combining dipole and quadrupole operators that yield greater classical Fisher information than the optimized dipole readout considered here. For ensembles of up to 17 spins, their disorder-averaged CFI surpasses the standard quantum limit at both disorder strengths studied, including a regime where the dipole readout remains below it. For the larger ensembles studied, fixing the encoding axis to the direction that maximizes the disorder-averaged quantum Fisher information retains nearly the same performance. These results identify a route to extracting metrological information from frequency-disordered spin ensembles through the choice of collective observable.
summary: This theoretical study develops a method to recover quantum metrological advantage in spin ensembles suffering from static frequency disorder. Using Bayesian Optimization, the authors find that optimizing the readout to include quadrupole terms, beyond simple dipole measurements, significantly boosts the extractable Fisher information. This demonstrates a robust pathway for high-precision quantum sensing in noisy, disordered quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to effectively extract metrological information from squeezed spin states when the system is corrupted by static local frequency disorder.
main_result: By employing Bayesian Optimization to select a collective readout observable combining dipole and quadrupole operators, the achievable classical Fisher information consistently surpasses the standard quantum limit and outperforms simpler dipole-only readouts.
method: The core method involves using Bayesian Optimization to search for the optimal collective readout observable, maximizing the disorder-averaged classical Fisher information calculated from the full measurement-outcome distribution.
model_or_system: The system modeled is an interacting ensemble of spin-1/2 particles ($N$ spins) governed by a Hamiltonian that includes a disorder term ($\delta	ilde{\omega}(i)$) representing static local frequency inhomogeneity.
key_observables: Classical Fisher Information ($\overline{F}C$), Quantum Fisher Information ($\overline{F}Q$), and the Wineland Squeezing Parameter ($\xi_R^2$).
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($r$), number of spins ($N$), and the comparison between rank-1 (dipole) and rank-2 (dipole+quadrupole) readouts.
main_assumptions: The reported values are the 'best values found' via BO and do not constitute a proof of global maxima; the analysis is restricted to a specific family of collective observables.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of achievable CFI vs. N for different disorder strengths, showing the recovery of metrological advantage (crossing the SQL) with optimized readouts, and comparing the performance of different readout types.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of disorder-induced decoherence, introduces the BO framework for optimizing collective readouts, presents quantitative results comparing rank-1 vs. rank-2 observables, and concludes by identifying the optimal observable structure.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, computationally guided protocol for mitigating environmental noise (frequency disorder) in quantum sensing platforms, which is highly relevant for experimental implementations using trapped ions or superconducting qubits.
